sources.title: SAFE Huifa [2020] No. 14 — Current-Account FX Business Guidelines (2020), State Council Gazette
sources.read: Arts. 54–56, 59–62, 64–65, 68, 86, 89: quota of USD 50,000 a year for settlement by any individual and for purchase by a 境内个人; a 境外个人 buys FX against documented lawful China-source current-account RMB income with ID plus source material including tax vouchers; splitting and quota borrowing lead to the watch list; cash carry limits.

sources.title: Bank of China FX quotation board (USD row, 2026-11-10 17:39:58 Beijing time)
sources.read: Per USD 100: spot buy 665.71, spot sell 668.51, cash sell 668.51, BOC conversion rate 671.67. The page states the board is for reference and the rate actually dealt governs.

sources.title: IRS — Gifts from foreign person (Form 3520)
sources.read: Report gifts or bequests from a nonresident alien or foreign estate only if the aggregate exceeds USD 100,000 in the tax year; purported gifts from foreign corporations or partnerships above USD 20,116 (2025) / USD 20,573 (2026).

sources.title: Bank of China — e-banking personal transfer and remittance tariff (standard from 2014-11-01)
sources.read: Cross-border wire: 1‰ of the amount, minimum CNY 50, maximum CNY 260 per wire, plus cable fee CNY 150 (CNY 80 for Hong Kong, Macao, Taiwan). Local differences and discounts may apply.

sources.title: SAFE Hebei branch — service guide: emigrant property transfer approval (2024-08-16)
sources.read: Conditions, documents, 20 working days, no fee, one visit, result is a single-use approval valid nationwide; quotes PBOC Announcement [2004] No. 16 Art. 2 and the 2024 Capital-Account Guidelines 6.4.

sources.title: SAFE Guizhou branch — service guide: inheritance property transfer approval (2025-05-19)
sources.read: Foreign citizens remit a lawfully inherited China estate after approval by the SAFE branch of the deceased's last household registration; documents; 20 working days; no fee.

sources.title: SAFE Anhui branch — operating guidelines annexed to Huifa [2025] No. 43 (2025-09-25)
sources.read: Foreign individual selling a China home: the amount remitted may not exceed the sale price less the taxes of that sale and may not exceed the amount on the tax certificate; title must already be transferred; refunds of failed purchases go back the way they came, with reasonable interest.

sources.title: Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations (State Council Order No. 532, 2008)
sources.read: Arts. 39, 40, 45: fine up to 30% of the amount, and 30% up to the full amount in serious cases, plus criminal liability; Art. 42: warning and fine up to 20% for carrying FX across the border in breach; Art. 48: fine up to CNY 50,000 for an individual who submits untrue documents; Art. 52: definition of 境内个人.

sources.title: State Council Order No. 851 (2026-10-29) — latest decision amending and repealing regulations
sources.read: Amends 14 regulations and repeals 4; the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations are not among them.

sources.title: IRS — Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR)
sources.read: A US person files FinCEN Form 114 if foreign accounts exceeded USD 10,000 in aggregate at any time in the year; due April 15 with automatic extension to October 15; filed through FinCEN, not with the tax return.

sources.title: IRS — Summary of FATCA reporting for U.S. taxpayers (Form 8938)
sources.read: Living in the US, unmarried: more than USD 50,000 on the last day of the year or USD 75,000 at any time; joint: USD 100,000 / 150,000. Living abroad: USD 200,000 / 300,000; joint: USD 400,000 / 600,000.

sources.title: 26 U.S.C. §988 — Treatment of certain foreign currency transactions (U.S. Code, GPO)
sources.read: (c)(1)(C): disposing of nonfunctional currency, including foreign-currency bank deposits, is a section 988 transaction; (e)(2): an individual's personal transaction recognises no exchange-rate gain unless the gain exceeds USD 200.

sources.title: STA and SAFE Announcement 2013 No. 40 — tax filing for outward payments (current text)
sources.read: A single outward payment above USD 50,000 for listed items (a foreign individual's China work pay, dividends, interest, property-transfer income and others) requires a tax filing; if tax was not paid, it is collected. Art. 4: foreign individuals follow the individual FX rules.

sources.title: STA and SAFE Guoshuifa [2005] No. 13 — tax certificate for individual property transfers abroad
sources.read: An existing tax-payment voucher can be given directly; no tax certificate is needed when the property to be transferred totals CNY 150,000 or less; unpaid tax may be declared and paid, after which the certificate is issued.

sources.title: SAFE — Q&A on Huifa [2017] No. 29 (overseas cash withdrawals with domestic bank cards)
sources.read: All cards of one person together: at most CNY 100,000 equivalent per calendar year; CNY 10,000 equivalent per card per day; exceeding the annual amount suspends overseas withdrawals for that year and the next; card spending abroad does not use the USD 50,000 purchase quota.

sources.title: State Taxation Administration — Individual Income Tax Law (2018 amendment, English text)
sources.read: Art. 1: 183-day residence test; Art. 2: nine categories of taxable income; Art. 3: 3–45% on comprehensive income, 5–35% on business income, flat 20% on interest, dividends, leasing, transfer of assets and incidental income; Art. 6: how taxable income is computed.

sources.title: PBOC Decree [2006] No. 3 — Measures for the Administration of Individual Foreign Exchange
sources.read: Art. 13: a 境外个人 may buy and remit FX against lawful current-account RMB income earned in China; Art. 26: property transfers abroad follow the property-transfer rules; Art. 37: 境内个人 = Chinese citizens holding a PRC ID, 境外个人 = foreign citizens holding passports.

sources.title: PBOC and seven other agencies — Yinfa [2026] No. 42 on virtual-currency risks (2026-02-06)
sources.read: Exchanging legal tender and virtual currency in China is an illegal financial activity and strictly prohibited; financial institutions may not provide accounts or transfers for it; repeals Yinfa [2021] No. 237.

sources.title: IRS — Foreign currency and currency exchange rates
sources.read: Amounts on a US return are in US dollars; foreign-currency income is translated at the exchange rate prevailing when it is received, paid or accrued.

sources.title: Wise Help Centre — Guide to CNY transfers (provider's own page)
sources.read: Sending from CNY: not for mainland Chinese nationals; you work or have worked in China; a China tax record from the last 3 years; only to an account you own; CNY 300,000 per transfer from a bank app; overall limit is after-tax China salary. No fee figure is stated on the page.

sources.title: IRS Publication 54 — Tax Guide for U.S. Citizens and Resident Aliens Abroad
sources.read: A US citizen's worldwide income is generally subject to US income tax wherever they live; foreign income tax paid may be claimed as a foreign tax credit on Form 1116.

sources.title: SAFE Huifa [2014] No. 2, as amended — SAFE Tianjin branch posting (2024-09-03)
sources.read: Art. 6: approval by the SAFE branch of the former household registration; the staged-remittance requirement for emigrants is abolished, so the bank may remit once or in several payments within the approved amount; notarisation of title documents and agency papers no longer required.

sources.title: U.S. Customs and Border Protection — Money and Other Monetary Instruments
sources.read: Currency or monetary instruments exceeding USD 10,000 carried into or out of the United States must be reported on FinCEN Form 105; the threshold applies to a family or group together; unreported currency can be seized.

sources.title: IRS news release IR-2026-48 — remittance transfer tax
sources.read: From 2026-01-01 a 1% tax applies to remittances sent from the United States to foreign recipients when the sender pays with cash, a money order, a cashier's check or a similar physical instrument.

sources.title: Chase — Chase Secure Banking page, footnote on incoming wires
sources.read: Domestic and international incoming wires have a USD 15 fee per transfer; other institutions may deduct processing fees from the wire amount.
